summary_hint: <source_form> K-1 for tax year <tax_year>: <partner_or_shareholder_name> owns <ownership %> of <entity_name> (EIN <entity_ein>); ordinary income <box 1>, guaranteed payments <guaranteed_payments>, distributions <distributions> — the K-1 amounts IN-12 rolls into qualifying income.

typed_core.name: tax_year
typed_core.why: IN-12 — the year the amounts cover; disambiguator beside every figure; multi-year averaging

typed_core.name: source_form
typed_core.why: IN-12 — 1065 (partnership) vs 1120S (S-corp): the qualifying-income methodology differs; also which boxes carry income
typed_core.prompt_hint: Read from the header: 'Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)' = partnership; 'Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S)' = S-corp. The form governs box numbering and the income method

typed_core.name: final_or_amended_k1
typed_core.why: processor — an AMENDED K-1 supersedes; a FINAL K-1 signals the entity/interest ended (continuance)

typed_core.name: entity_name
typed_core.why: IN-12 — match the entity to the business tax return / CPA letter / business license

typed_core.name: entity_ein
typed_core.why: PII (masked, EIN) — entity identity; match key across business documents

typed_core.name: entity_address
typed_core.why: identity — entity location; corroborates the business

typed_core.name: partner_or_shareholder_name
typed_core.why: IN-12 — must be the borrower; attributes the income

typed_core.name: partner_or_shareholder_tin
typed_core.why: PII (raw, highly_restricted) — borrower SSN/TIN; match key
typed_core.prompt_hint: Treat the partner/shareholder TIN as a raw SSN — never quote it

typed_core.name: partner_or_shareholder_address
typed_core.why: identity/occupancy; PII — borrower address, must be typed or it lands unmasked in the catch-all

typed_core.name: partner_type_or_shareholder_status
typed_core.why: processor/IN-12 — general vs limited partner changes self-employment-tax treatment of the income

typed_core.name: profit_loss_capital_or_ownership_percentages
typed_core.why: IN-12 — the ownership share(s) used to attribute entity income; profit/loss/capital % can differ

typed_core.name: current_year_net_income_or_loss
typed_core.why: IN-12 — the partner's share of net income/loss

typed_core.name: capital_account_ending
typed_core.why: processor — ending capital; supports capital-account and viability analysis

typed_core.name: withdrawals_and_distributions
typed_core.why: IN-12 — distributions from the capital-account section (Item L); qualifying income per the example

typed_core.name: guaranteed_payments
typed_core.why: IN-12 — guaranteed payments to the partner count as self-employment income

typed_core.name: distributions
typed_core.why: IN-12 — box distributions (1065 box 19 / 1120S box 16 code D); the example's 'K-1 distributions → qualifying income'

nested_lists.name: k1_box_items
nested_lists.shape_reason: a K-1 carries many numbered boxes (ordinary income, net rental, interest, dividends, capital gain, §179, credits, and lettered sub-codes) — many items, so a flat row is light and stays well under the 16,384 ceiling

fields.name: amount
fields.why: IN-12 — the box amount (the calculator reads ordinary business income box 1, rental box 2, and others)

fields.name: code
fields.why: IN-12 — the lettered code where present

fields.name: source
fields.why: provenance — the section/box the value came from

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: classification/version before extraction; source_form identifies the schedule

rejected.name: issuer_name
rejected.reason: duplicates entity_name (the entity issues the K-1)

rejected.name: issuer_address, issuer_phone, issuer_email_or_url
rejected.reason: not on a K-1 / marginal; catch-all

rejected.name: document_issue_date, effective_date, expiration_date
rejected.reason: a K-1 reports a completed tax year; tax_year is the period

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: covered by entity_ and partner_ flattened fields

rejected.name: ownership_change_dates
rejected.reason: rarely present; no IN-12 gate; catch-all

rejected.name: capital_account_beginning, capital_contributed
rejected.reason: intermediate rollforward lines; ending capital + distributions suffice; catch-all

rejected.name: partner_share_of_liabilities
rejected.reason: CONDITIONAL; not a direct income input; catch-all

rejected.name: state_and_local_k1_items
rejected.reason: state overlay; no IN-12 (federal) gate; catch-all

rejected.name: attached_statements
rejected.reason: supporting statements; captured by reference; catch-all

encoding_variations: source_form — read from the K-1 header: 'Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)' = partnership; 'Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S)' = S-corp. The form governs box numbering (e.g. distributions are 1065 box 19 vs 1120S box 16 code D) and the income method

ownership percentages — 1065 Item J shows beginning/ending profit, loss, and capital % (which can differ); 1120S shows a single stock-ownership %. No percent coercer; flatten to str and keep all stated percentages

distributions appear twice — in the capital-account rollforward (Item L 'withdrawals & distributions') and in the box section (box 19 / 16D). Keep both; they can differ and the calculator may use either — the disambiguator is which section each came from
final_or_amended_k1 / domestic-foreign — checkboxes at the top; degrade to str
partner_type — 'General partner or LLC member-manager' vs 'Limited partner or other LLC member'; affects SE-tax treatment

open_questions.recommendation: flat-row, comfortably under the ceiling (box counts are moderate-to-many with lettered sub-codes) GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Distributions duplication — the capital-account distribution (Item L) and the box distribution (19/16D) can differ
options: type both (chosen) and let IN-12 pick
open_questions.recommendation: type both — the discrepancy is itself informative; keep the section as the disambiguator

open_questions.q: Ownership % degradation — profit/loss/capital % differ and there is no percent coercer; flattened to one str
options: confirm which numeric % IN-12 uses (typically profit %)
open_questions.recommendation: keep the str now, flag the numeric need

open_questions.q: PII registration — entity_ein, partner_or_shareholder_tin, and partner_or_shareholder_address are all unregistered under these names
open_questions.recommendation: confirm registration before go-live so the snapshot masks them

notes: Decision-critical amounts (guaranteed_payments, distributions, current_year_net_income_or_loss) are ALSO typed above because IN-12 uses them directly; k1_box_items carries the remaining boxes so none are lost to the discarded catch-all.
IN-12 rolls up ordinary business income (box 1), net rental (box 2/3), guaranteed payments (1065 box 4), and distributions (1065 box 19 / 1120S box 16 code D).
Ambiguity: partner_type_or_shareholder_status is tagged 'processor/IN-12' — classed processor as primary but it also serves IN-12 (SE-tax treatment of income); flagged.
